newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Guardian PMPA pretax profit drops to 64mln punts.
newsitem.headline: Guardian PMPA pretax profit drops to 64mln punts.

text.p: Guardian PMPA on Tuesday showed a sharp drop in pre-tax profit to 64.3 million Irish pounds in 1996 compared to 105.1 million in 1995.

The group said in a results statement that the drop in operating profit to 42.1 million punts, down from 59 million in 1995, was due to a downturn in the underwriting result which slipped to a loss of 4.9 million in 1996 from a profit of 11.3 million in 1995.
"Our performance in 1996 was very strong despite the worsening trends in claims costs and accident frequency which seriously impacted on our underwriting performance," Guardian PMPA said.
Guardian PMPA said premium income increased by almost six percent during the year to 317.1 million punts from 300.3 million and underlying premiums grew five percent.
Net written premiums for non-life business was 220.6 million punts up from 210.5 million and Life premiums were marginally higher at 14.3 million up from 14 million.
It said foreign non-life business grew to 82.2 million punts from 75.8 million in 1995.

Guardian said the overall underwriting environment in 1996 could be characterised as "difficult and challenging" due primarily to a significant increase in the number and cost of claims and excessive competition in the market.
"Pricing is a key issue ... and is one that is being determined by the way claims costs develop and investment markets perform," Guardian PMPA said.
It said at present claims costs are rising at a level well ahead of normal inflation while investment returns are declining.
Guardian PMPA is the Irish unit of Guardian Royal Exchange Group.
